q: Which real-world activity best represents the Input-Process-Output (IPO) cycle taught in Grade 3 computer classes?
a: Washing dirty clothes in a washing machine to get clean clothes
w: Reading a storybook aloud to a classmate during free time
Looking at a painting displayed on a classroom wall
Sleeping at night to feel energetic the next morning
e: Dirty clothes act as input, washing acts as processing, and clean clothes are the output.

q: A Grade 3 student claims that a cartoon movie playing on a monitor is computer hardware. How should the teacher correct this misconception?
a: The monitor is hardware, but the movie is software data displayed on it.
w: The movie is hardware because it can be seen clearly on screen.
Both the physical monitor and the movie are software.
The movie becomes hardware once it is saved permanently on a hard disk.
e: Hardware refers to physical parts like the monitor, while the movie is digital content.

q: Which device functions strictly as an input device for a desktop computer system?
e: A barcode reader only feeds optical data into the computer system.

q: Which memory component loses its stored data as soon as the computer is turned off?
e: RAM is volatile memory that clears completely when power is disconnected.

q: In MS Paint, which tool is specifically designed to sample a color from one part of a drawing and apply it to another?
e: The Color Picker tool picks up an exact color shade from an image for reuse.

q: When typing a paragraph in MS Word, which key moves the blinking cursor to the beginning of the next line?
e: The Enter key creates a line break and moves the insertion point to the next line.

q: What happens when a student presses Ctrl + Z while editing a document in MS Word?
a: The last action performed is canceled.
w: The entire document is saved to disk.
Selected text is copied to clipboard.
The document is sent to the printer.
e: Ctrl + Z is the standard keyboard shortcut to undo the most recent action.

q: Why is sequential order essential when writing an algorithm for a task like making a cup of tea?
a: Executing steps out of order leads to an incorrect outcome.
w: Computers can only process algorithms written in English.
Algorithms are invalid if they contain more than three steps.
Order does not matter as long as all steps are present.
e: An algorithm requires logical step-by-step sequencing to achieve the correct result.

q: In a standard flowchart taught in primary school, which shape represents a decision or condition check?
e: A diamond symbol indicates a decision point branching into alternative paths.

q: Which shape is universally used to represent the Start and Stop points in a simple flowchart?
e: An oval symbol serves as the start and end terminator in flowcharts.

q: In Scratch programming, what is the default character object that appears on the Stage called?
e: Programmable characters or objects on the Scratch stage are called sprites.

q: A Scratch script has three blocks stacked vertically: when green flag clicked, move 10 steps, and say Hello!. What happens when the green flag is clicked?
a: The sprite moves 10 steps first and then displays the speech bubble Hello!.
w: The sprite displays Hello! before moving 10 steps forward.
The sprite moves and speaks simultaneously in a loop.
The code fails because motion blocks cannot follow flag blocks.
e: Scratch executes connected blocks sequentially from top to bottom.

q: Which rule represents a safe practice for Grade 3 students browsing the internet?
a: Keep personal details private from online strangers.
w: Share account passwords with classmates for group work.
Click on pop-up boxes offering free game gifts.
Accept video call requests from unknown online users.
e: Protecting personal identity and credentials is vital for internet safety.

q: Which analogy best explains the relationship between a file and a folder to a primary school student?
a: A file is like a sheet of paper, and a folder is like a binder holding papers.
w: A file is a large cabinet, while a folder is a single paper inside it.
A file holds computer programs, while a folder holds physical hardware.
A file is hardware, whereas a folder is software.
e: A folder acts as a digital container that organizes individual files.

q: A student asks whether an ATM screen that responds to finger touches is an input or an output device. What is the correct response?
a: It acts as both input when touched and output when displaying information.
w: It is strictly an input device because user touch is recorded.
It is strictly an output device because visual screens only show text.
It is neither input nor output, but a processing device.
e: Touchscreens act as dual-purpose devices combining touch input with visual output.

q: What is the primary function of an Operating System like Windows on a computer?
a: It manages computer hardware and helps run application programs.
w: It creates artwork and edits photos created by users.
It connects physical wires from the monitor to the main box.
It cleans dust from internal electronic components.
e: The Operating System is the master software controlling hardware and user applications.

q: In basic spreadsheet software like MS Excel, what is the intersection of a column and a row called?
e: The rectangular box formed by the intersection of a row and column is a cell.

q: When maintaining a computerized list of student details, what term describes all collected information about one specific student?
e: A record contains the complete set of related data fields for a single entry.

q: Why should open water bottles and snacks be kept away from computer tables in the lab?
a: Accidental spills can short-circuit internal electronic circuits.
w: Food crumbs reduce the internet speed of the computer system.
Spilled liquids cause digital viruses to infect computer software.
Keyboards automatically disable themselves near food items.
e: Liquids conduct electricity and cause severe damage by short-circuiting electronic components.

q: If a desktop computer does not turn on when the power button is pressed, what initial step should a teacher guide students to take?
a: Check if the power cord is properly plugged into the electrical outlet.
w: Reinstall the main operating system software immediately.
Replace the internal mouse connection cord.
Delete old files from the secondary hard disk.
e: Basic troubleshooting begins with checking primary physical power connections.

q: Which software program is classified as application software rather than system software?
e: MS Paint is an application created for specific drawing tasks, whereas Windows, Linux, and macOS are operating system software.

q: Which computer device is used primarily for storing large amounts of permanent data rather than displaying output?
e: A hard disk drive stores files permanently, whereas monitors, speakers, and projectors function as output devices.

q: A student wants to type a single capital letter 'T' at the start of a word without locking all future letters in uppercase. Which key combination should be used?
e: Holding the Shift key while typing a letter capitalizes only that specific letter without enabling Caps Lock.

q: When a student saves a picture drawing created in MS Paint, which file extension is commonly assigned to save the drawing format?
e: MS Paint typically saves graphics using image extensions like .png or .bmp.

q: What happens when a user double-clicks directly on a word inside an MS Word document?
e: Double-clicking a word in MS Word selects that specific word.

q: Which text formatting option slants typed text to the right to make it stand out?
e: The Italic command slants selected text to the right for emphasis.

q: In computational thinking, what term describes repeating a set of step-by-step instructions multiple times?
e: Looping, or iteration, is the process of repeating instructions until a specified condition is met.

q: In a standard introductory flowchart, which geometric shape represents taking input or displaying output?
e: A parallelogram symbol indicates input operations and output displays in standard flowcharts.

q: Which flowchart shape is used to represent an action step or calculation such as adding two numbers?
e: A rectangle represents processing steps or calculations in a flowchart.

q: In Scratch 3.0, what action occurs when a script runs the block move -10 steps?
e: A negative value in a move block causes the sprite to move backward relative to its direction.

q: Under which block category in Scratch 3.0 can a teacher find the block when space key pressed?
e: Blocks that trigger scripts based on user interactions like key presses belong to the Events category.

q: How can a Grade 3 student create the illusion of a walking character animation in Scratch?
w: Hide and show the sprite rapidly without delay
e: Alternating between different costume poses in a loop produces smooth character animation.

q: Which item of information is suitable for a student to share on a public school hobby website?
e: General preferences like a favorite cartoon are non-sensitive, whereas home addresses and passwords must remain private.

q: What is the recommended action for a Grade 3 student who receives an unkind message online?
a: Tell a parent or teacher immediately
e: Students should report cyberbullying or unkind online content directly to a trusted adult.

q: In a simple class data table, what term describes a single column containing one category of information like Student Name?
e: In basic data handling, a vertical column storing a specific attribute is called a field.

q: In basic spreadsheet applications, how are columns designated across the top header row?
e: Spreadsheet columns are identified by letters (A, B, C), while rows are identified by numbers.

q: What is the main physical benefit of keeping back straight and feet flat on the floor while using lab computers?
a: It prevents muscle strain and maintains posture
w: It makes the computer process data faster
It prevents the screen from flickering
It protects keyboard keys from wear
e: Good seating posture prevents strain on the spine and muscles during extended computer use.

q: Which internal hardware unit is responsible for executing instructions and performing math calculations in a computer?
e: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) functions as the main processor for instructions and calculations.

q: How does the action of the Backspace key differ from the Delete key when editing text?
a: Backspace erases to the left; Delete erases to the right
w: Backspace erases full lines; Delete erases single characters
Backspace saves text; Delete removes the page
Backspace moves cursor up; Delete moves cursor down
e: Backspace removes the character immediately to the left of the cursor, whereas Delete removes the character to the right.

q: Which tool in MS Paint allows a user to zoom in on a small section of a drawing for fine editing?
e: The Magnifier tool enlarges specific regions of the canvas for detailed drawing adjustments.

q: A student points to a mouse pad and asks if it is computer hardware. How should the teacher clarify this?
a: It is a physical accessory, not an electronic component of the computer system.
w: It is input hardware because it directly feeds position data to the monitor.
It is storage hardware because it holds the mouse steady during typing.
It is output hardware because it guides the movement of the screen pointer.
e: Accessories like mouse pads are physical items but not electronic hardware components of the computer system.

q: What is the primary action performed when a user holds down the left mouse button while moving the mouse across a surface?
e: Holding the left mouse button while moving the mouse is called dragging, used to move objects or select text.

q: Which portable storage device uses flash memory and plugs directly into a USB port to transfer files between school computers?
e: A pen drive (USB flash drive) is a portable flash-based storage device that connects via a USB port.

q: Which keyboard shortcut key combination selects all text and graphics in an active MS Word document?
e: Ctrl + A is the standard keyboard shortcut used to select all content in a document or window.

q: A student wants to fill a completely closed rectangular shape with yellow color in MS Paint. Which tool must be used?
e: The Fill with Color tool floods an enclosed area with the selected foreground color.

q: Which text alignment option distributes typed text evenly between the left and right margins of a document?
e: Justify alignment adjusts spacing so text aligns flush along both left and right margins.

q: What is the main purpose of an algorithm in elementary computing?
a: To provide a step-by-step set of instructions to complete a specific task.
w: To translate binary numbers directly into human-readable text.
To repair damaged hardware components inside the computer system.
To display colorful graphic graphics and animations on the screen.
e: An algorithm is a clear, step-by-step procedure or set of rules designed to accomplish a task.

q: In a standard flowchart, what do the directional arrow lines connecting geometric shapes represent?
e: Flow lines with arrows indicate the sequence or flow of control from one step to the next.

q: Where does a sprite position itself on the Scratch Stage when its X and Y coordinates are both set to 0?
a: At the exact center of the Stage
w: At the top-left corner of the Stage
At the bottom-left corner of the Stage
At the top-right corner of the Stage
e: In Scratch, the coordinate point X: 0, Y: 0 corresponds to the exact center of the Stage.

q: In Scratch 3.0, under which color-coded block category can a student find blocks to play audio or alter pitch?
e: Audio and sound effect controls in Scratch are located under the magenta-pink Sound category.

q: Which software application is specifically designed to access, retrieve, and view web pages on the Internet?
e: A web browser (such as Chrome or Firefox) is an application used to render and display web pages.

q: Which practice creates a secure password for a student account?
w: Using the student's date of birth
e: Strong passwords combine uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols rather than personal details.

q: In basic spreadsheet software like MS Excel, how are horizontal rows labeled along the left border?
e: Spreadsheet rows are identified by numbers (1, 2, 3...), while columns are identified by letters (A, B, C...).

q: Which type of computer system is designed to stay in one fixed location and requires constant wall power?
e: Desktop computers are stationary systems that rely on a continuous direct AC electrical outlet power source.

q: In elementary data management, what term describes re-arranging a list of names in alphabetical order?
e: Sorting is the process of arranging data records in a specific sequential order, such as alphabetical.

q: Why should students always turn off a computer using the operating system's Shut Down option?
a: It allows the system to save data and safely close running applications.
w: It recharges the internal backup battery of the monitor display unit.
It prevents dust from entering the ventilation holes of the computer casing.
It automatically deletes all unused files from the primary hard disk.
e: Using the proper Shut Down option ensures open files are saved and operating system files close safely.

q: In MS Paint, which command allows a user to save an already saved file with a new name or in a new folder?
e: Save As prompts the user for a new name or folder location, creating a separate file copy.

q: Which font formatting effect in MS Word draws a horizontal line through middle of selected text?
e: Strikethrough creates a horizontal line through the center of selected characters.

q: Which output device converts a digital document displayed on screen into physical printed paper?
e: A printer takes digital soft-copy data and produces physical hard-copy printouts on paper.

q: In Scratch 3.0, under which category can a block be found that checks if a sprite is touching the mouse-pointer?
e: Blocks that detect collisions, key presses, or mouse interactions are located in the light-blue Sensing palette.

q: A student stores a project on a USB pen drive to bring it to school. What type of storage device is a pen drive?
e: A pen drive is an external secondary storage device used for saving data permanently.

q: Which flowchart symbol represents a decision-making step where the path splits based on a condition?
e: A diamond shape is used in flowcharts to test conditions and branch into alternative paths.

q: In Scratch visual programming, which block category contains the command block used to change a sprite position by moving it forward?
e: Motion blocks control sprite movement and positioning on the stage.

q: In Microsoft Word, what is the main effect of pressing Ctrl + B on selected text?
w: It opens the find dialog box.
e: Ctrl + B is the standard keyboard shortcut to apply or remove bold style.

q: What is the recommended action for a student who receives a message from an unknown person online asking for personal details?
e: Primary internet safety guidelines require children to report unknown online contacts to adults.

q: Which component of the Windows desktop displays open applications and allows quick switching between them?
e: The taskbar shows running programs and allows users to switch between open windows.

q: In standard flowcharting, which shape represents taking input from a user or displaying output?
e: A parallelogram is used specifically to denote input and output operations in flowcharts.

q: In a spreadsheet program like Microsoft Excel, how is the cell located in column D and row 7 identified?
e: Cell references combine column letters followed by row numbers.

q: Which of the following is categorized as System Software rather than Application Software?
e: An operating system is system software that controls basic hardware operations.

q: What is the default visual character object present on the stage in Scratch called?
e: In Scratch, movable graphics or objects controlled by scripts are called sprites.

q: Why is RAM classified as volatile memory?
a: Its contents are lost when power is turned off.
w: It can only be read and never written.
It runs slower than secondary storage.
e: Volatile memory requires continuous electrical power to retain stored data.

q: Which function key starts a slide show presentation from the very first slide in Microsoft PowerPoint?
e: Pressing F5 initiates the presentation from slide one in PowerPoint.

q: A student wants to transfer a file from Folder A to Folder B so that it no longer exists in Folder A. Which commands should be used?
e: Cut removes the original file and Paste places it in the new destination.

q: Which application software is specifically designed to access and view websites on the World Wide Web?
e: A web browser retrieves and displays web pages from the internet.

q: What is the primary objective of creating an algorithm before coding?
a: To outline a logical step-by-step solution to a problem
w: To translate high-level code into binary
To draw graphics for the screen layout
e: An algorithm is a step-by-step plan created to solve a problem systematically.

q: Which unit of the Central Processing Unit performs arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons?
e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) executes mathematical operations and comparisons.

q: Which control block in Scratch should be used to repeat a set of code blocks a fixed number of times, such as 4 times?
e: The repeat block executes its nested blocks for a specified count.

q: What constitutes a strong password practice for user accounts?
a: Using a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols
w: Using your date of birth and first name
Writing it on a note attached to the screen
e: A strong password combines diverse character types and must remain confidential.

q: Which paragraph alignment option aligns text evenly along both the left and right margins in MS Word?
e: Justify alignment adjusts character spacing so text touches both margins evenly.

q: In spreadsheet programs, what character must always be typed first to indicate that a cell entry is a formula?
e: An equal sign tells the spreadsheet to compute the entry as a mathematical formula.

q: Which component of the Central Processing Unit acts as a supervisor and manages the flow of data and instructions between all parts of the computer?
e: The Control Unit coordinates and manages all operations within the computer system.

q: Which key combination in MS Word allows a user to reverse the last action performed in a document?
e: Ctrl + Z is the standard shortcut to undo the most recent action in Microsoft Word.

q: What is the main purpose of creating a subfolder inside a main folder on a computer drive?
a: To organize files systematically into smaller logical groups
w: To compress files to save disk space
To prevent files from being infected by viruses
To automatically back up files to the internet
e: Subfolders help users organize files logically into specific categories within a main folder.

q: In MS PowerPoint, which feature is used to apply a visual movement effect to an individual text box or object on a slide?
e: Animations are visual effects applied to individual objects on a slide, whereas transitions apply to whole slides.

q: In a standard computer flowchart, which geometrical shape represents a processing or calculation step?
e: A rectangle is used to denote processing steps such as calculations or variable assignments in a flowchart.

q: In Scratch, which event block is commonly used to trigger a script when the user starts the program execution?
e: The 'when green flag clicked' block serves as the standard starting trigger for scripts in Scratch.

q: Which non-volatile primary memory stores permanent instructions required to boot up a computer system?
e: Read-Only Memory (ROM) is non-volatile memory containing permanently written setup instructions like startup code.

q: In MS Excel, which built-in function is used to calculate the total sum of numbers present in a specified range of cells?
e: The SUM function adds all the numerical values present within the selected range of cells.

q: What term refers to a scam where fraud artists send fake messages to trick users into revealing sensitive data like passwords?
e: Phishing is a cyber attack technique where fraudulent communications trick users into revealing confidential personal data.

q: Which system software component directly manages hardware devices and acts as an interface between user applications and system hardware?
e: The operating system manages computer hardware resources and provides common services for user application software.

q: In MS Word, which formatting tool allows a user to copy formatting settings from one selected text selection and apply it to another?
e: Format Painter copies all formatting options from selected text and applies them to target text.

q: What default behavior occurs in Scratch when a sprite is commanded to move continuously towards the edge of the stage without edge detection blocks?
a: It partially hides at the stage border
w: It disappears permanently from the project
The program crashes with an error
e: By default, Scratch prevents sprites from leaving the stage completely by stopping them partially at the border.

q: What is the global unique address used to identify a specific document or web page on the World Wide Web?
e: Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is the web address used to locate a specific web page online.

q: Which computer device creates physical hard-copy documents by transferring ink or toner onto paper?
e: A printer converts digital data from a computer into physical hard copies on paper.

q: What term describes a finite sequence of step-by-step logical instructions written to solve a specific computational problem?
e: An algorithm is a logical set of step-by-step instructions designed to accomplish a given task.

q: What is the basic container box formed by the intersection of a vertical column and a horizontal row in MS Excel called?
e: A cell is the fundamental unit of a worksheet created by the intersection of a column and a row.

q: Which view in MS PowerPoint displays all slides as small thumbnail versions on a single screen for quick reorganization?
e: Slide Sorter view displays all slides as thumbnails so users can easily reorder or organize them.

q: Which peripheral device captures physical photographs or printed text and converts them into digital images for computer processing?
e: A scanner reads physical photos or paper documents and converts them into digital files.

q: What term defines the acceptable code of polite and responsible behavior that users should follow while communicating on the internet?
e: Netiquette combines network and etiquette to define acceptable conduct when interacting online.

q: In Scratch programming, under which block category would you find commands to change a sprite's visual costume or backdrop?
e: The Looks category contains commands related to changing costumes, backdrops, and visual appearance of sprites.

q: Which early mechanical calculating device designed by Charles Babbage is considered the historical precursor to modern general-purpose digital computers?
e: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine with an ALU, control flow, and memory, making it the concept model for general-purpose computers.

q: Which group of keys on a standard keyboard includes Shift, Ctrl, and Alt, which are used in combination with other keys to modify their action?
e: Keys like Shift, Ctrl, and Alt are called modifier keys because they modify the normal action of another key when pressed together.

q: What primary information does a filename extension, such as .docx or .png, provide to the operating system?
a: The file format and which application should open it
w: The physical storage location on the hard drive
The total memory size occupied by the file
The user permission and password protection level
e: File extensions identify the internal data format of a file and tell the operating system which program to use to open it.

q: What happens to an application window when a user clicks the Minimize button in Windows?
a: It hides from the desktop screen and stays open on the taskbar.
w: It closes permanently and clears from RAM.
It resizes to fill the entire desktop monitor.
It deletes the active file saved inside the application.
e: Minimizing an application window hides it from view while keeping the application running in active memory accessible via the taskbar.

q: In MS Word formatting, what is the main difference between Subscript and Superscript options?
a: Subscript drops text below the baseline while superscript raises it above.
w: Subscript changes font size while superscript changes font style.
Subscript underlines text while superscript strikes through text.
Subscript capitalizes letters while superscript makes letters lowercase.
e: Subscript places text slightly below the normal line of typing, whereas superscript places text slightly above it.

q: In MS PowerPoint, what distinguishes a Slide Transition from an Animation effect?
a: Transition applies to slide movement while animation applies to slide objects.
w: Transition changes slide colors while animation changes font styles.
Transition plays audio files while animation plays video clips.
Transition works automatically while animation requires internet access.
e: Transitions control how entire slides enter or exit during a presentation, whereas animations control the motion of individual objects on a single slide.

q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between data and information?
a: Data is unorganized raw facts, whereas information is processed meaningful data.
w: Data is processed output, whereas information is raw user input.
Data is stored permanently, whereas information exists only in RAM.
Data refers to text, whereas information refers exclusively to images.
e: Data consists of unprocessed numbers, characters, or facts, while information is structured and processed data that carries context and meaning.

q: In Scratch visual programming, what occurs on the stage when a sprite moves after running the pen down command block?
a: It leaves a continuous drawn line along the path traveled by the sprite.
w: It erases all background colors present on the stage.
It creates clone duplicates of the sprite along its path.
It hides the sprite graphic completely from the stage visual.
e: The pen down block activates the drawing feature of a sprite so that any movement leaves a visible line trace on the stage.

q: Which type of computer network is designed to connect devices across a short distance within a single classroom or school building?
e: A Local Area Network (LAN) connects computers and peripheral devices within a limited geographical area such as a school or office.

q: By default in Microsoft Excel, how are text values and numeric values aligned inside a cell?
a: Text is left-aligned and numbers are right-aligned.
w: Text is right-aligned and numbers are left-aligned.
Text is center-aligned and numbers are right-aligned.
Text is left-aligned and numbers are center-aligned.
e: Excel automatically aligns text entries to the left edge of a cell and numerical values to the right edge.

q: Why is it recommended for young students to use a screen nickname instead of their full real name on public online educational forums?
a: To protect personally identifiable information from being publicly accessible
w: To increase the download speed of the web browser
To prevent computer viruses from infecting the operating system
To enable automatic spell checking on posted messages
e: Using handles or pseudonyms prevents strangers on the internet from identifying and contacting students in the real world.

q: In standard flowchart diagramming, which geometric shape represents the Start or End point of a process flow?
e: An oval symbol (or rounded rectangle) represents the start or stop terminal points of a flowchart algorithm.

q: While typing text in MS Word, what does a red wavy underline beneath a word signal to the user?
e: MS Word uses a red wavy line to highlight words that are not recognized in its standard dictionary, indicating a possible spelling error.

q: In standard computer binary memory measurement, how many Bytes make up exactly 1 Kilobyte (KB)?
e: In computing binary standards, 1 Kilobyte equals 2 to the power of 10, which is 1024 Bytes.

q: Which computer port is commonly used to transmit both high-definition video and multi-channel digital audio over a single cable to a monitor?
e: High-Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) carries uncompressed digital video and audio signals together through one cable.

q: In MSW Logo, which command sequence correctly instructs the turtle to draw a complete square with sides of length 100 units?
e: A square has 4 equal sides and 90-degree right-angle turns, so repeating FD 100 and RT 90 four times draws a square.

q: In Scratch, how does the behavior of a repeat 10 block differ from a forever block during execution?
a: repeat 10 stops after ten iterations, while forever loops until manually stopped.
w: repeat 10 executes code faster than a forever block.
repeat 10 works only with movement blocks, while forever works with all blocks.
repeat 10 runs automatically, while forever requires a key press event.
e: The repeat block executes its nested code a fixed number of times, whereas the forever block loops endlessly until script termination.

q: Which of the following file extensions identifies a standard digital audio sound file?
e: .mp3 is a widely used digital audio coding format, whereas .png and .bmp are image formats and .docx is a text document format.

q: Which posture adjustment helps prevent neck strain when working at a desktop computer for schoolwork?
a: Positioning the top of the monitor screen at or slightly below eye level
w: Placing the keyboard above shoulder height while typing
Bending forward so eyes are five inches from the display screen
Tilting the screen upwards at a steep angle toward ceiling lights
e: Aligning the top of the screen at or just below eye level keeps the neck in a neutral, relaxed position to reduce physical strain.

q: When a user deletes a file from a local hard disk folder using the standard Delete key in Windows, where is it stored temporarily?
e: Deleted files from a local drive are moved to the Recycle Bin, allowing users to restore them if deleted accidentally.

q: A Grade 5 student asks why BIOS instructions are stored in ROM instead of RAM. Which explanation is correct?
a: ROM retains its stored instructions even when the computer power is turned off.
w: ROM can store much larger files than RAM.
ROM allows faster editing of data during system startup.
RAM is reserved only for running audio and video drivers.
e: ROM is non-volatile memory that retains essential boot setup instructions even when power is disconnected.

q: Which of the following is classified as system software rather than application software?
e: An operating system is system software that manages computer hardware, whereas word processors and browsers are application software.

q: Which file extension indicates an executable program file in a Microsoft Windows environment?
e: The .exe file extension stands for executable and is used to launch application programs in Windows.

q: In standard flowcharting for computer science, which geometric shape represents a decision-making step?
e: A diamond symbol in a flowchart denotes a conditional point where a yes/no branch occurs.

q: Which flowchart symbol correctly represents inputting data or displaying output?
e: A parallelogram is the standard flowchart symbol for input and output operations.

q: In Scratch programming, what happens when a student places a move 10 steps block inside a repeat 10 block?
a: The sprite moves 10 steps ten separate times in sequence.
w: The sprite moves 10 steps once and stops.
The sprite moves 100 steps in a single frame.
The sprite turns 10 degrees ten times.
e: The repeat block executes the enclosed move block sequentially for the specified 10 iterations.

q: What are the x and y coordinates of the exact center of the stage in Scratch?
e: The origin point at the center of the Scratch stage is defined by coordinates x = 0 and y = 0.

q: A student types 5 + 5 into cell A1 of a spreadsheet, but it displays 5 + 5 instead of 10. What did the student omit?
a: An equals sign at the beginning of the cell entry
e: Spreadsheets require an equals sign (=) at the start of an entry to evaluate it as a formula.

q: In a spreadsheet, what does the cell reference address C4 represent?
e: Spreadsheet cell addresses list the column letter first followed by the row number.

q: Which practice demonstrates strong account security when creating passwords?
a: Combining uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols
w: Using your full name combined with your date of birth
Reusing the same simple password across all personal accounts
Sharing your password with your classmate for safe keeping
e: Strong passwords use a mix of character types to make guessing or cracking them difficult.

q: A student receives an email asking them to click a link to claim a free prize by submitting private personal details. What is this tactic called?
e: Phishing involves tricking users into providing sensitive personal information by pretending to be a trustworthy entity.

q: Which network type is used to connect computers within a single computer lab or school building?
e: A Local Area Network (LAN) covers a small, limited geographical area like a single school room or building.

q: What is the primary role of the Recycle Bin in Windows?
a: Temporarily storing deleted files until permanent removal
w: Scanning deleted files for software viruses
Compressing large system files to free up disk space
Automatically creating cloud backups of user documents
e: The Recycle Bin holds deleted files temporarily, allowing users to restore them if needed.

q: What is the output of the Python expression: math.ceil(-4.2)?
e: math.ceil returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to x, which for -4.2 is -4.

q: Which HTTP status code signifies that a client request was successfully processed by the web server?
e: HTTP status code 200 OK indicates a successful HTTP request.

q: What is the standard base case condition for calculating the factorial of a non-negative integer n recursively?
e: Factorial of 0 and 1 are both 1, making n <= 1 the base case to stop recursive calls.

q: Which SQL keyword is placed immediately after SELECT to suppress duplicate rows from the query results?
e: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result set.

a: Moves the file pointer to the end of the file
w: Moves the file pointer to the beginning of the file
